standards_at_play.version: v1.0.2 (unverified: the record on file is a search result, not a fetched specification)
standards_at_play.governs: the shape and identity of any message entering the platform, whichever producer sent it
standards_at_play.what_it_fixes: gives every intake a uniform (id, source, subject) identity so one envelope covers a command line, a repository event, an HTTP request and a schedule
standards_at_play.what_it_leaves_open: carries no actor, no delegation chain, no budget ceiling and no run-tree grouping key; the correlation carrier per boundary is left to the platform
standards_at_play.quote: Producers MUST ensure that source + id is unique for each distinct event.

standards_at_play.governs: an outside agent submitting work and following its lifecycle, and the identity of a run that pauses and resumes
standards_at_play.what_it_fixes: a named task state machine and a stable (taskId, contextId) pair, so a paused run resumes as itself rather than as a new run
standards_at_play.what_it_leaves_open: says nothing about pricing before commitment, budget ceilings, or what a refusal body contains
standards_at_play.quote: A2A v1.0 defines a full Task state machine with nine named states

standards_at_play.governs: one prompt turn against an agent runtime and the reason the turn stopped
standards_at_play.what_it_fixes: makes the agent runtime a class rather than a product: a turn, a stop reason, a cancel
standards_at_play.what_it_leaves_open: fixes no budget, no identity and no correlation on the turn; measured here to mint its own root trace rather than continue an injected one
standards_at_play.quote: The Agent Client Protocol (ACP) is an open JSON-RPC standard for connecting code editors to AI coding agents.

standards_at_play.governs: how a unit of work reaches a tool, and the per-call version discipline every capability interface here should copy
standards_at_play.what_it_fixes: a published tool surface plus a version declared per request rather than agreed once per session, with a stated deprecation window
standards_at_play.what_it_leaves_open: registers no tools by itself; the endpoint here is live and empty
standards_at_play.quote: every request declares its protocol version through the io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion key in its _meta field

standards_at_play.governs: whether a declared document, envelope or record may enter at all
standards_at_play.what_it_fixes: one published dialect for every shape the platform ships, checkable by a validator nobody here wrote
standards_at_play.what_it_leaves_open: validates structure, not truth: a well-formed document can still declare a definition of done that nothing can fail
standards_at_play.quote: The current version is 2020-12

standards_at_play.governs: every refusal at every boundary
standards_at_play.what_it_fixes: one machine-readable failure object with a type URI, so a caller branches on a type and never on wording
standards_at_play.what_it_leaves_open: defines the container, not the registry: the closed set of type URIs this platform answers with is ours to write
standards_at_play.quote: RFC 9457 defines a "problem detail" to carry machine-readable details of errors in HTTP response content

standards_at_play.governs: the transport and shape of every span, metric and log the platform emits
standards_at_play.what_it_fixes: a stable transport for three signals, so the collector behind it is the safest swap on the board
standards_at_play.what_it_leaves_open: carries whatever attributes it is given; it does not decide what correlates a run
standards_at_play.quote: The current OTLP specification version available is 1.11.0.

standards_at_play.governs: the attribute vocabulary for agent, model and tool work
standards_at_play.what_it_fixes: one vocabulary spanning agent, workflow and tool steps rather than a house name per step kind
standards_at_play.what_it_leaves_open: is not stable, has no multi-agent session attribute, and must therefore be versioned separately from the transport
standards_at_play.quote: not one is marked Stable

standards_at_play.version: v1.3.0 released 2025-11-04 (unverified); PASS.md names the spec without a version
standards_at_play.governs: how a unit of work is contained while it runs
standards_at_play.what_it_fixes: states containment as declared resources and declared egress, satisfied today by hardware virtualisation and tomorrow by something else
standards_at_play.what_it_leaves_open: says nothing about who may run inside, whose quota a slot draws from, or what a containment report must assert
standards_at_play.quote: The OCI Runtime Spec v1.3.0 was released on November 4, 2025

standards_at_play.governs: how a unit of work asks for inference
standards_at_play.what_it_fixes: a de facto request shape every gateway and serving engine already speaks, so a caller names a class and not a vendor
standards_at_play.what_it_leaves_open: its own batch route branches on vendor names and refuses one that is in use here, so provider-specific passthrough is not portable
standards_at_play.quote: Callers request a class, never a vendor.

standards_at_play.governs: whether an action is permitted, decided before spend
standards_at_play.what_it_fixes: a JSON-in / JSON-out decision contract, which is exactly what makes the engine behind it swappable
standards_at_play.what_it_leaves_open: a decision API that nothing calls changes nothing: the checks exist here and are not in the enforcement path
standards_at_play.quote: OPA evaluates the input against the specified policies to return an access decision in JSON

standards_at_play.standard: in-toto Statement v1 in a DSSE envelope, with SLSA predicates
standards_at_play.governs: attribution of every artifact to the code version, inputs and actor that produced it
standards_at_play.what_it_fixes: a three-layer attestation verifiable with third-party tooling, which is the whole point of the provenance concern
standards_at_play.what_it_leaves_open: attests artifacts well and agent actions less well; a run-shaped predicate for an agent action is not settled
standards_at_play.quote: The embedded attestation in the dsse envelope includes a "_type" field set to "https://in-toto.io/Statement/v1".

standards_at_play.governs: the delegation chain every action carries
standards_at_play.what_it_fixes: an existing encoding for an explicit chain of actors, current actor outermost, least recent most deeply nested
standards_at_play.what_it_leaves_open: does not say what roots the chain; a chain whose last hop is a name the caller supplied for itself is rooted in nothing
standards_at_play.quote: A chain of delegation can be expressed by nesting one act claim within another.

standards_at_play.governs: the root of the delegation chain for a non-human actor
standards_at_play.what_it_fixes: a short-lived credential issued only after the workload is attested against platform facts, so identity is not a field a caller asserts
standards_at_play.what_it_leaves_open: no identity field exists anywhere in the system today, so there is nothing to migrate from
standards_at_play.quote: SPIRE attests a workload against platform facts

standards_at_play.governs: when a schedule fires, expressed portably
standards_at_play.what_it_fixes: one portable string for a repeating schedule, so the thing that fires it is an adapter and not the definition
standards_at_play.what_it_leaves_open: a recurrence rule is not an occurrence: it says nothing about the identity, budget or replay-safety of the run a firing starts
standards_at_play.quote: An RRULE is the recurrence rule grammar defined in RFC 5545

standards_at_play.governs: whether an externally triggered action is safe to replay
standards_at_play.what_it_fixes: one key on the wire with a stated uniqueness obligation on the producer
standards_at_play.what_it_leaves_open: the convention is a header, not a store: a key with no lease behind it deduplicates nothing, which is the state here
standards_at_play.quote: The idempotency key MUST be unique and MUST NOT be reused with another request with a different request payload.

standards_at_play.version: unversioned (released as an open standard 2025-12-18; unverified)
standards_at_play.governs: how a reusable unit of capability is packaged and discovered
standards_at_play.what_it_fixes: one portable directory shape any conformant runtime can load, with a bounded resident cost
standards_at_play.what_it_leaves_open: the format is not published as an explicitly versioned artifact, so the version has to live in the registry record instead
standards_at_play.quote: Anthropic does not currently publish the skill format as an explicitly versioned artifact.

standards_at_play.standard: RFC 9162 Merkle log with RFC 8785 JSON canonicalization
standards_at_play.governs: the integrity mechanism under the state seam and the audit trail
standards_at_play.what_it_fixes: inclusion and consistency proofs over an append-only log, and a canonical byte form to hash, so verification is cheaper than rescanning the chain
standards_at_play.what_it_leaves_open: tamper-evident is not tamper-proof: the guarantee only lands if something independently monitors the log
standards_at_play.quote: RFC 9162 defines an append-only Merkle log with inclusion and consistency proofs.

standards_at_play.governs: what a person watching or answering a run receives, as typed events rather than raw output
standards_at_play.what_it_fixes: a typed event stream with an interrupt model, so the surface a person holds can crash or be replaced between the ask and the decision
standards_at_play.what_it_leaves_open: no version record is on file, and it fixes the wire, not who is allowed to answer a gate
standards_at_play.quote: an open, lightweight, event-based protocol that standardizes how agents connect to user-facing applications

standards_at_play.governs: resolving a capability or a server by name and version rather than by path
standards_at_play.what_it_fixes: prior art for a signed, versioned, content-addressed record served over a stable API
standards_at_play.what_it_leaves_open: still in preview; and a registry record is not the same as the packaging format it points at
standards_at_play.quote: The Registry API has entered an API freeze (v0.1)

standards_at_play.governs: whether a caller can integrate without a client library this platform wrote
standards_at_play.what_it_fixes: machine-readable descriptions that make design rule 4 checkable instead of aspirational
standards_at_play.what_it_leaves_open: a description proves a shape, not that all four entries behave identically once driven
standards_at_play.quote: OpenAPI for REST APIs and AsyncAPI for event-driven APIs provide machine-readable specifications

standards_at_play.standard: Durable execution: no standard to adopt
standards_at_play.governs: a multi-step unit of work surviving a crash and resuming at the first incomplete step
standards_at_play.what_it_fixes: nothing: this is one of the two boundaries PASS.md names as having no specification to take whole
standards_at_play.what_it_leaves_open: everything - step, key, checkpoint and resume point have to be written here, and written so a queue plus a state machine can satisfy them
standards_at_play.quote: Two boundaries have no standard to adopt.

standards_at_play.standard: State persistence: no standard to adopt
standards_at_play.governs: how the graph and the ledger persist
standards_at_play.what_it_fixes: nothing published; the hash chain in place is the idea worth keeping
standards_at_play.what_it_leaves_open: the write model, concurrency, integrity mechanism, retention and the planner's query surface are all ours to specify
standards_at_play.quote: The chain is the valuable idea and should survive; the file is not.

standards_at_play.standard: Agent memory: no ratified standard found
standards_at_play.governs: what a run is allowed to remember between runs
standards_at_play.what_it_fixes: nothing: the only protocol on file is a preprint proposal
standards_at_play.what_it_leaves_open: scope, staleness, supersession and provenance of a memory item are designed here, which makes memory a third design-ourselves seam beside the two PASS.md names
standards_at_play.quote: no prior protocol provides verified memory portability

standards_at_play.standard: Saga / compensating transaction pattern: a pattern, not a standard
standards_at_play.governs: undoing the part of a run that already had an effect
standards_at_play.what_it_fixes: a named shape - every forward action node maps to a backward compensating node, run in reverse order
standards_at_play.what_it_leaves_open: no published contract, and no universal undo: some effects can only be compensated and some cannot be taken back at all
standards_at_play.quote: A compensating transaction is a new operation that is the logical inverse of the one it undoes.

state_types.state: entry envelope - the one record a producer's message is normalised into
state_types.home_today: absent as a record: PASS.md B3 names four intake adapters and no envelope they share
state_types.home_ideal: the work-intake capability, written once at admission and never re-derived downstream
state_types.written_by: the driving adapter for the entry that received the message
state_types.pinning_risk: Pins to whichever producer was built first if the envelope grows a field only one producer can fill; the adapter boundary keeps the producer's native payload on the far side of a mapper and lets a fifth producer cost a mapping table rather than a new door.
state_types.quote: Four entries cover nearly every situation: a human, an event, a schedule (time), and an external system or agent. All four enter through the same shape.

state_types.state: document - declared intent, definition of done, steps, addressed by the digest of its canonical form
state_types.home_today: absent: PASS.md names the Document as a target core component, not a Part A component
state_types.home_ideal: the core, as data with no service behind it; validated through the document-validation capability
state_types.written_by: the entry adapter that framed the caller's intent
state_types.pinning_risk: Pins if a component enriches or rewrites the document on the planner's behalf, because planning then depends on that component; the adapter boundary is that validation is imported and the document is immutable once declared.
state_types.quote: data — declared intent, definition of done, steps

state_types.state: resolved manifest and effective configuration - the values a run actually resolved, per layer
state_types.home_today: absent, and measured to be dangerous: configuration written in the documented place was silently discarded
state_types.home_ideal: an attestation emitted by each adapter at start-up, recording what it resolved rather than what it was handed
state_types.written_by: each adapter, at resolution time
state_types.pinning_risk: Pins to a component's own configuration layering when the platform trusts the file rather than the resolved value; the adapter boundary is that the adapter must report its effective configuration, so a silent overlay is detectable rather than believed.
state_types.quote: Values written to YAML validated, reviewed correctly, and had no runtime effect.

state_types.state: plan and cost - the priced decomposition of a document, produced before anything is spent
state_types.home_today: absent: PASS.md names the Planner as a target core component
state_types.home_ideal: the core, as a pure function of the document and inputs pinned at one state head
state_types.written_by: the planner
state_types.pinning_risk: Pins the moment pricing requires calling the thing being priced; the adapter boundary is that cost inputs are values passed in, not clients the planner holds.
state_types.quote: pure function `document → plan + cost`

state_types.state: cost inputs pinned at a head - price table and historical cost quantiles a plan was derived from
state_types.owner_capability: core planner, over the state seam's query surface
state_types.home_today: absent
state_types.home_ideal: the state seam, read once at a pinned head and recorded by digest on the plan
state_types.written_by: whoever publishes the cost table; read-only to the planner
state_types.pinning_risk: Pins to a gateway's own pricing API if read live; the adapter boundary is that the table is data at a pinned head, so a change of estimate is a change of data rather than of code.
state_types.quote: the query surface a planner needs

state_types.state: work graph - typed nodes and typed edges (existence, interface, implementation)
state_types.home_today: absent: PASS.md names the Graph as a target core component
state_types.home_ideal: the core, persisted as a projection of the state seam's log rather than as its own store
state_types.written_by: the planner, when a plan resolves
state_types.pinning_risk: Pins if an executor's own DAG type becomes the graph; the adapter boundary is that the graph is a fold over appended facts, so the executor holds no nodes of record.
state_types.quote: typed nodes, typed edges (existence / interface / implementation)

state_types.state: assumption / open claim - a structural decision named, assumed against a contract, and validated later
state_types.owner_capability: core graph and core planner (late binding)
state_types.home_today: absent; the reference records the whole mechanism as missing here
state_types.home_ideal: the document, with the area of effect computed over implementation edges by the graph
state_types.written_by: the caller, in an assumptions block
read_by: human gate when the decision returns a tradeoff
state_types.pinning_risk: Pins to whichever engine was assumed if the interface cannot actually hold both candidates; the adapter boundary is the stated contract the candidates sit behind, and a plan is refused when that contract cannot hold.
state_types.quote: the whole late-binding mechanism

state_types.state: dispatch record - one unit of agent work, its ceilings, its stop reason and its outputs
state_types.home_today: three implementations and no contract between them
state_types.home_ideal: the dispatch seam, as the one request-and-result shape every runtime is reached through
state_types.standard: none published; A2A task states and RFC 9457 refusals are borrowed shapes (unverified)
state_types.written_by: the dispatcher
state_types.pinning_risk: Pins to whatever executes the unit if the request carries a runtime's own fields; the adapter boundary is that the request names a unit and its ceilings and never a machine configuration.
state_types.quote: It must specify: the request shape, the result shape, cancellation semantics, timeout and budget enforcement, partial-result handling, and what a failure returns.

state_types.state: agent turn and its context - one prompt turn, what it received, what it folded back, and every compaction in between
state_types.home_today: the agent runtime in the microVM, driven over ACP as JSON-RPC over stdio
state_types.home_ideal: the agent-runtime capability, with the context contract declared on the dispatch request
state_types.standard: Agent Client Protocol (unverified); no standard for the context contract
state_types.written_by: the runtime adapter
state_types.pinning_risk: Pins to an interactive runtime if streaming, tool-permission callbacks or a live session are required rather than negotiated; the adapter boundary makes every interactive capability optional and absent by default so a one-shot runner can serve.
state_types.quote: Compaction is the practice of taking a conversation nearing the context window limit, summarizing its contents, and reinitiating a new context window with the summary.

state_types.state: isolation admission and containment report - declared resources, declared egress, and what was asserted from outside the unit
state_types.home_today: one microVM per agent, guest network none, dummy guest credential, per-VM uid jail
state_types.home_ideal: the isolation capability, taking a document handle and a declaration and never an agent or a tool surface
state_types.written_by: the isolation adapter at admission
state_types.pinning_risk: Pins to hardware virtualisation if the declaration carries boot arguments, a block-device layout or a guest kernel; the adapter boundary is resources and egress only, so a weaker containment technology resolves to a weaker profile rather than an unparseable request.
state_types.quote: `0700`, owned by a per-VM uid with no passwd entry — verified live

state_types.state: model routing selection and claim ticket - which class was asked for, what it resolved to, and the outstanding future for a slow answer
state_types.home_today: one gateway over 25 groups, each carrying a scoped virtual key with a hard budget cap
state_types.home_ideal: the model-access capability, with routing a pure function evaluated in front of the adapter
state_types.written_by: the routing function, then the model-access adapter
state_types.pinning_risk: Pins the moment a request field names a vendor, a member model or an endpoint - the failure has already happened here, where the standard's own batch route branches on three provider names and refuses a fourth; the adapter boundary is that the class prefix is the entire routing vocabulary a caller has.
state_types.quote: Batch runs through Gemini's native `:batchGenerateContent` via LiteLLM passthrough

state_types.state: workflow step and checkpoint - a step id, its idempotency key, its checkpoint reference and the resume point
state_types.home_today: the workflow orchestrator has its data directory present and nothing listening
state_types.home_ideal: the durable-execution capability, expressing step, key, checkpoint and resume point and nothing else
state_types.written_by: the durable-execution adapter, committing the checkpoint with the step's own effect
read_by: operator asking where a run stopped
state_types.pinning_risk: Pins to a replay engine if the contract mentions deterministic workflow code, worker registration or an event-history format; the adapter boundary is a record, not an engine, so a row committed beside the effect satisfies it too.
state_types.quote: Durable workflow orchestration and human-in-the-loop signals are designed around it and it is currently down

state_types.state: loop iteration - attempt N of M, why it re-ran, and which of the three terminations ended the loop
state_types.owner_capability: loop composition over dispatch, judge and budget
state_types.home_today: gap
state_types.home_ideal: the loop composition, with one iteration as one durable step keyed by loop id and iteration index
state_types.written_by: the loop operator
state_types.pinning_risk: Pins to an executor's own retry primitive if the iteration is not a first-class record; the adapter boundary is that a loop reaches dispatch, grading, checkpointing and the ceiling only through capability interfaces.
state_types.quote: `stop` firing means done. `cap` firing means escalate.

state_types.state: fan-out unit share and failure tolerance - the per-unit slice of a ceiling and how many units may fail
state_types.home_today: gap
state_types.home_ideal: the budget guarantee, with the share on the step and the tolerance on the fan-out
state_types.written_by: the planner, when a fan-out resolves
state_types.pinning_risk: Pins to whatever runs the fan-out if tolerance is expressed as that engine's retry policy; the adapter boundary is that tolerance is a property of the fan-out, not of the unit and not of the plan.
state_types.quote: Failure tolerance is a property of the fan-out, not the unit and not the plan.

state_types.state: parked approval - the gate, the ask it emitted, the decision that came back, and the deadline on it
state_types.owner_capability: human interaction, with the gate declared by the approval composition
state_types.home_today: a host unit that approves, rejects or returns a parked workflow from a phone; the signals it was designed around are down
state_types.home_ideal: the human-interaction capability, with the parked state owned by the platform rather than by whoever holds the screen
state_types.standard: A2A task states and a typed elicitation shape (unverified); AG-UI for the stream (unverified)
state_types.written_by: the composition that declared the gate
read_by: budget (a parked gate accrues no spend)
state_types.pinning_risk: Pins to one decision surface if the ask is a message on that surface rather than a record; the adapter boundary is that the ask carries a response schema and the decision is matched to the run's own correlation id, so the surface can crash or be replaced between them.
state_types.quote: the action can be approved as-is (approve), modified before running (edit), rejected with feedback (reject), or responded to directly (respond)

state_types.state: working memory - what one run is currently holding in context, including its compaction transitions
state_types.owner_capability: memory (working scope), bounded by the agent-runtime context contract
state_types.home_today: gap
state_types.home_ideal: the dispatch request and result, as declared context in and folded summary out
state_types.written_by: the runtime adapter and the dispatcher
state_types.pinning_risk: Pins to a runtime's own conversation store if context is implicit; the adapter boundary is that every compaction is a recorded transition naming its strategy and the tokens before and after.
state_types.quote: Context folding is a mechanism that allows agents to actively manage their working context via branching and folding

state_types.state: episodic memory - what happened in earlier runs, retrievable and expirable
state_types.home_today: gap
state_types.home_ideal: the memory capability, every item carrying scope, provenance and a staleness policy at write time
state_types.written_by: the unit of work that observed it
read_by: later runs at the same scope
state_types.pinning_risk: Pins to a vector store if the interface carries an embedding, a similarity threshold, a k or an index name; the adapter boundary is that a caller names a scope and a need, and ranking belongs to the adapter.
state_types.quote: raw episodic data should always carry one

state_types.state: long-term memory - durable claims about the world, superseded rather than edited
state_types.home_today: gap
state_types.home_ideal: the memory capability, with active supersession on write so two versions of a fact are never both recallable
state_types.written_by: the unit of work that concluded it
state_types.pinning_risk: Pins to whichever store is chosen if supersession is implemented as an update; the adapter boundary is that a correction is a new item and the superseded one stays readable to provenance.
state_types.quote: active supersession on every write so contradictions never accumulate

state_types.state: ledger record - the append-only record across runs, and the deduplication authority
state_types.owner_capability: core ledger over the state seam
state_types.home_today: a hash-chained JSONL task store whose closing digest opens the next run
state_types.home_ideal: the state seam, as one log of immutable facts that both the graph and the ledger fold over
state_types.standard: none published; RFC 9162 and RFC 8785 are the integrity primitives (unverified)
state_types.written_by: the platform, on the one append path
read_by: planner asking whether work already happened
state_types.pinning_risk: Pins to a file format if readers join a path rather than query a projection; the adapter boundary is the record and the named projections, so an object store, a relational store or an event log can serve.
state_types.quote: each run's closing digest is the next run's opening digest, so a manual edit between runs is detectable

state_types.state: state head and run seal - the pinned head every read is taken at, and the sealed head that closes a run
state_types.home_today: the closing digest of a run, in the hash-chained store
state_types.home_ideal: the state seam: resolve_head is the only call whose answer moves
state_types.written_by: the state seam on append and on seal
state_types.pinning_risk: Pins to a single-writer file if concurrency is solved by locking one process; the adapter boundary is a conditional append naming the head it expects, which a store with a uniqueness constraint enforces without locks.
state_types.quote: The UNIQUE (stream_id, version) constraint is load-bearing.

state_types.state: redaction tombstone - a body removed while its digest and every proof over it still verify
state_types.home_today: absent: retention is named as something the state seam must specify and is not specified
state_types.home_ideal: the state seam, as a tombstone that preserves the record digest
state_types.written_by: the redacting authority, recorded
state_types.pinning_risk: Pins to a store that cannot delete without breaking its chain, forcing a choice between compliance and integrity; the adapter boundary is that the chain commits to the digest of the canonical body and never to the body.
state_types.quote: This must specify: the write model, concurrency and single-writer guarantees, the integrity mechanism, retention, and the query surface a planner needs.

state_types.state: provenance attestation - an artifact bound to the code version, inputs and actor that produced it
state_types.home_today: an append-only evidence store naming script hash, git commit, tree hash and whether the tree was dirty
state_types.home_ideal: the provenance capability, emitting a signed statement in an envelope a third-party tool can verify
state_types.standard: in-toto Statement v1 in DSSE, with SLSA predicates (unverified)
state_types.written_by: the platform, at the close of a unit of work
state_types.pinning_risk: Pins to a house record format if verification needs a tool we wrote; the adapter boundary is the envelope and predicate, so the store behind it can be a file, a transparency log or an attestation service.
state_types.quote: Each record names the script SHA-256, git commit, tree hash under test, and whether the tree was dirty.

state_types.state: budget reservation and spend - one ceiling per root unit, the slice each descendant drew, and the reconciled figure
state_types.home_today: a scoped virtual key with a hard budget cap per model group, verified to terminate spend rather than merely record it
state_types.home_ideal: the budget guarantee, enforced outside the unit that spends, at the enforcement chain's reserve slot
state_types.written_by: the enforcement chain, before the thing it wraps begins
read_by: the caller reading a cap escalation
state_types.pinning_risk: Pins to a gateway's own key model if the ceiling only exists as that gateway's budget; the adapter boundary is a reservation and a draw held by the platform, so a per-key cap becomes one enforcement point among several rather than the definition.
state_types.quote: Every unit of work carries a ceiling. Exceeding it terminates the unit, not the platform

state_types.state: identity and delegation chain - who is acting, on whose behalf, and what rooted the chain
state_types.home_today: absent
state_types.home_ideal: bound at entry by the driving adapter, onto the envelope, before any planning or spend
state_types.standard: OAuth 2.0 Token Exchange act claims, over an attested workload root (unverified)
state_types.written_by: the driving adapter at the entry point
state_types.pinning_risk: Pins to one identity provider if the chain is that provider's token; the adapter boundary is a claim structure the dispatch carries and does not define, so the issuer can change without changing what a hop is.
state_types.quote: No identity field anywhere in the system

state_types.state: mandate / credential - a scope-limited, expiring authorization to spend, deploy or send, and the real secret behind it
state_types.home_today: the real key is held by a host-side broker reached over vsock; the guest holds a dummy key
state_types.home_ideal: the mandate-broker capability, exchanging an actor's identity for a short-lived credential scoped to one destination
state_types.written_by: the broker, on exchange
state_types.pinning_risk: Pins to one transport if the credential path assumes vsock and a host process; the adapter boundary is that the unit asks for a destination and receives a scoped credential, never a key, so a hosted sandbox with no host broker can serve the same interface.
state_types.quote: vsock → host broker, which holds the real key and picks the endpoint

state_types.state: policy decision - a deterministic refusal recorded before execution, at each of the enforcement points
state_types.home_today: a policy engine is in the stack, and conformance checks exist that are not wired into the enforcement path
state_types.home_ideal: the policy capability behind a decision API, called from the enforcement chain at admission, at dispatch and at every model or tool call
state_types.standard: Rego / OPA decision API, JSON in and JSON out (unverified)
state_types.written_by: the enforcement point that took the decision
state_types.pinning_risk: Pins to one policy language if the decision input is that language's document; the adapter boundary is a JSON request and a JSON decision, which is what lets a different engine answer.
state_types.quote: Conformance checks exist; not wired into the enforcement path

state_types.state: evaluation case set, verdict and baseline - a versioned corpus, a three-valued outcome, and the stored baseline it is compared against
state_types.home_today: absent; the nearest thing is a pipeline measured to run green with every behavioural stage skipped
state_types.home_ideal: the evaluation capability, offline and dev-time, distinct from the runtime judge
state_types.standard: GenAI conventions carry a result, they do not produce one (unverified)
state_types.written_by: the evaluation harness, appending never overwriting
read_by: capability registry before a version is promoted
state_types.pinning_risk: Pins to one harness if a metric class, a dataset loader or a test-runner decorator appears in a core signature; the adapter boundary is a case set reference and a report, so a replay harness and a live harness both serve.
state_types.quote: Only diff, syntax and format ran. Those establish well-formedness, not correctness.

state_types.state: registry record and version - a capability or agent resolved by name and a version constraint, signed and digest-matched
state_types.home_today: capability packages resolved as files on disk
state_types.home_ideal: the capability-registry capability, records immutable and resolution by name and constraint only
state_types.standard: packaging is unversioned, so the version lives in the registry record (unverified)
state_types.written_by: whoever publishes a version
read_by: every resolution of a skill, workflow, loop or agent
state_types.pinning_risk: Pins to a directory layout the moment any component joins a path to reach a capability; the adapter boundary is that the same name and constraint returns the same record from any conformant store.
state_types.quote: Mutable metadata are represented as new versioned records rather than in-place edits

state_types.state: agent profile record - what an agent is good at, what it is not for, its model class, tools, shapes and concurrency
state_types.owner_capability: capability registry, declared by the agent composition
state_types.home_today: gap
state_types.home_ideal: a registry record, so a caller resolves a name and a constraint and gets the profile back
state_types.standard: an agent card is the published shape for describing another party's agent (unverified)
state_types.written_by: whoever declares the agent
state_types.pinning_risk: Pins to one runtime if the profile names a vendor model or that runtime's tool syntax; the adapter boundary is a model class and a declared tool list, resolved at admission.
state_types.quote: Each agent is defined up front by what it is good at, so callers know how to call it and how to sequence it.

state_types.state: telemetry span, metric and log record - what a step actually did, in a published vocabulary
state_types.home_today: an OTLP-native trace backend with its own storage, worker, queue and blob store
state_types.home_ideal: the telemetry capability, split into a pinned transport contract and a separately versioned attribute mapping
state_types.standard: OTLP 1.11.0 with GenAI semantic conventions at Development status (unverified)
state_types.written_by: the platform, on every operation; no caller may request or decline it
state_types.pinning_risk: Pins to one backend if emitters carry that backend's SDK types; the adapter boundary is the wire protocol, which is why this is the safest swap on the board.
state_types.quote: nothing. The safest swap

state_types.state: correlation record - the identifiers stamped at every boundary so a run can be reassembled
state_types.home_today: absent and measured to be broken: an injected trace context is ignored at the agent boundary and a depth-3 tree yields three unrelated root traces
state_types.home_ideal: stamped by the platform at dispatch as explicit resource attributes, re-stamped at every boundary, never inherited from ambient context
state_types.standard: OTLP resource attributes, declared unchangeable by the specification that defines them (unverified)
state_types.written_by: the platform, at each boundary crossing
state_types.pinning_risk: Pins to a tracing library's propagation if reassembly walks a parent chain; the adapter boundary is a stamped field set and a group-by, which survives a runtime that mints its own trace.
state_types.quote: A depth-3 task tree produces three unrelated root traces.

state_types.state: tenancy scope and quota - the principal every record, recall, spend and sandbox slot is bound to
state_types.home_today: absent as such; the nearest measured analogues are the per-VM uid jail and the per-group scoped keys with hard caps
state_types.home_ideal: bound at the identity slot as a property of the actor, checked at policy and drawn against at budget
state_types.written_by: the platform, at identity resolution
state_types.pinning_risk: Pins to whichever shared choke point enforces it first, usually a gateway key; the adapter boundary is that the principal rides on the actor, so every choke point checks the same value rather than each inventing its own.
state_types.quote: The best places to introduce noisy neighbor protections are at points in the architecture where tenants share resources

state_types.state: compensation record and irreversibility class - what a side-effecting step declared, and what undid it
state_types.home_today: gap
state_types.home_ideal: declared on the step in the document, executed in reverse order by the graph when a downstream step fails
state_types.standard: none; the saga pattern is prior art, not a specification
state_types.written_by: the step that declared it, and the orchestrator that ran it
state_types.pinning_risk: Pins to an engine's saga primitive if compensation is that engine's API; the adapter boundary is a declared compensating node on the graph, which any executor can walk.
state_types.quote: For every forward-facing action node in your graph, you must map a backward-facing compensating node

state_types.state: error / problem object - the one typed failure body every boundary returns
state_types.home_today: absent
state_types.home_ideal: one closed registry of type URIs, owned by the errors capability, carried by every capability's failure path
state_types.written_by: whichever boundary refused
state_types.pinning_risk: Pins to an adapter's native exception type if a failure is passed through untyped; the adapter boundary is that an untyped failure is itself reported as a registered adapter-unavailable problem and counted.
state_types.quote: Typed and machine-readable. Never parsed from prose

state_types.state: idempotency claim and lease - the key a repeat is recognised by, and the store that holds it
state_types.home_today: a key on the wire and no lease behind it
state_types.home_ideal: a keyed lease store called at every entry and at every step, with the key derived from the producer's own unique identity
state_types.written_by: the entry adapter, then the durable-execution step
state_types.pinning_risk: Pins to a durable engine if the lease is that engine's deduplication; the adapter boundary is claim(key, payload digest) returning fresh, duplicate or conflict, which a ledger or a keyed store can both answer.
state_types.quote: key on the wire, no lease

state_types.state: schedule occurrence - one firing of a recurrence rule, as a run with its own identity, ceiling and key
state_types.home_today: the orchestrator's schedules, on an orchestrator that is not listening
state_types.home_ideal: the scheduling capability, holding a portable recurrence rule and producing the same entry envelope as every other door
state_types.written_by: the scheduler adapter, at each firing
state_types.pinning_risk: Pins to one scheduler if the rule is that scheduler's syntax; the adapter boundary is a recurrence rule string plus an occurrence record, so cron or any conformant parser can fire it.
state_types.quote: RFC 5545 recurrence rules | Temporal schedules

state_types.state: event subscription - which producer's events reach which consumer, and on what filter
state_types.home_today: a repository-event intake adapter, provisioned as one of nine configuration roles
state_types.home_ideal: the work-intake capability, as a producer registered behind the existing door rather than a new door
state_types.written_by: whoever registers the subscription
state_types.pinning_risk: Pins to one broker if the subscription is that broker's object; the adapter boundary keeps entry categories a closed set of four and lets a new source arrive as an instance inside one of them.
state_types.quote: Entry categories are a closed set of four. What is inside each is open.

state_types.state: artifact and its digest - the output of a step, addressable and attributable
state_types.owner_capability: state persistence, with provenance over it
state_types.home_today: a blob store holds trace payloads; step artifacts as such have no named home in the inventory
state_types.home_ideal: the state seam for the reference and the digest, an object store for the bytes
state_types.written_by: the step that produced it
state_types.pinning_risk: Pins to a filesystem layout if artifacts are found by path; the adapter boundary is a digest-addressed reference recorded in the log, so the bytes can move without a reader changing.
state_types.quote: per-step artifact, verdict, usage

state_types.state: interface version declared per call - which revision of a capability interface a caller speaks
state_types.home_today: absent
state_types.home_ideal: declared on the call and refused per call, with a core field set frozen and a stated deprecation window
state_types.standard: the per-request version discipline in the tool-access protocol is the model (unverified)
state_types.written_by: the caller, on every call
state_types.pinning_risk: Pins the whole platform to one release train if a single version number covers every interface; the adapter boundary is one version per interface, so an attribute mapping can move faster than the transport that carries it.
state_types.quote: Deprecated features remain in the specification for at least twelve months.

tool_entries.adapter_boundary: Exposes: a routing class, a payload, a ceiling, and a claim ticket. Hides: which vendor, which member model, which endpoint, and which key paid for it.
tool_entries.must_stay_loose: The class prefix must stay the entire routing vocabulary a caller has, and routing must be a pure function evaluated in front of the adapter so it can be tested from a table.
tool_entries.would_pin: A request field that names a vendor, a member model or an endpoint; or a passthrough route only this gateway offers, which is how batch already runs here.
tool_entries.second_adapter: OpenRouter, direct provider SDKs, or a serving engine's native API
tool_entries.harness_minimal_call: Proposed: submit(class, payload, ceiling) and read one claim ticket, redeemed immediately by a fast adapter and later by a slow one.
tool_entries.quote: Model gateway — one OpenAI-compatible API over every provider

tool_entries.capability: model access (a coding CLI presented as a model class)
tool_entries.adapter_boundary: Exposes: a `cli-` class that answers like any other class. Hides: that a whole coding agent, not a model, produced the answer.
tool_entries.must_stay_loose: A caller must not be able to tell that this class is a CLI; the four `cli-` members must remain members of the same class vocabulary as the rest.
tool_entries.would_pin: A caller branching on the `cli-` prefix, or a field that only a CLI can honour, which would make this a second interface wearing one name.
tool_entries.harness_minimal_call: Proposed: the same submit call with a `cli-` class; nothing else changes.

tool_entries.must_stay_loose: The economics must stay behind the class: a caller asks for free and local, not for a GPU.
tool_entries.would_pin: A class whose meaning is a specific card, so the class cannot be served from anywhere else.
tool_entries.second_adapter: a hosted OpenAI-compatible server; caching behaviour differs per engine
tool_entries.harness_minimal_call: Proposed: submit with an `f-` class and accept that the ceiling may still refuse.

myopia_check.gap: A fifth caller exists that the four entries do not name: a running plan reporting a result back into work that already exists. It steers and never starts.
myopia_check.why_it_matters: If it is not named, either it is modelled as a sixth door and the closed set of four breaks, or it is modelled as an ordinary entry and a loop can mint its own root work with no actor above it and no ceiling to draw from.
myopia_check.proposed_owner: the work-intake capability, as an internal entry kind on the same envelope, refused at admission when it tries to start rather than steer

myopia_check.gap: The repository carries two different enumerations of the ways in - three (human, agent, internal or external event) and four (human, event, schedule, external system or agent) - and a reader cannot tell which one a statement is about.
myopia_check.why_it_matters: Every conformance claim about entry parity is ambiguous until one of the two is the normative list and the other is a mapping onto it.
myopia_check.proposed_owner: the consumption contract, which already states that a skill must name which enumeration it is citing
myopia_check.quote: Four entries cover nearly every situation

myopia_check.gap: Nothing above owns the view - the rendering a human decides from. It is a state type in its own right: a gate with no view is undecidable, and a person shown raw output has been given a transcript instead of a decision.
myopia_check.why_it_matters: The reference names a gate with no view as a resolve-time refusal and the repository records the required-view field as a gap here; without it every approval degrades to reading output.
myopia_check.proposed_owner: the human-interaction capability for the ask, and the approval composition for the required view field on the gate
myopia_check.quote: Decidable: every gate has a view

myopia_check.gap: Nothing owns the third resolution outcome for an open decision: confirmed, refuted, or a genuine tradeoff that no mechanism can settle.
myopia_check.why_it_matters: A framework that models a judgement as a boolean will silently record a decision nobody made.
myopia_check.proposed_owner: the graph, with the tradeoff outcome resolving to a human gate that renders the comparison
myopia_check.quote: will silently record a decision nobody made

myopia_check.gap: Nothing owns a deadline on an open assumption, so a plan can sit on a guess indefinitely.
myopia_check.why_it_matters: The hold state is what makes late binding survivable; without an expiry it becomes a way to never decide.
myopia_check.proposed_owner: the planner, checking assumption deadlines at resolve time alongside the depth bound
myopia_check.quote: nothing otherwise stops a plan sitting on a guess forever

myopia_check.gap: Nothing independently monitors the hash chain. The chain is verified by the same system that writes it.
myopia_check.why_it_matters: A tamper-evident log only delivers its guarantee when something outside it checks; a self-report that the log verified is not evidence.
myopia_check.proposed_owner: an audit-trail capability running as a scheduled entry, taking inclusion and consistency proofs from the state seam
myopia_check.quote: Transparency logs are tamper-evident but not tamper-proof

myopia_check.gap: No state type above existed for effective configuration until this blueprint added one, and it is the only measured failure of the three that has no owner at all.
myopia_check.why_it_matters: A value written in the documented place, validated and reviewed, had no runtime effect. Every other guarantee here is configured somewhere.
myopia_check.proposed_owner: an effective-configuration attestation emitted by each adapter at start-up (proposed capability; PASS.md B3 has no row for it)
myopia_check.quote: Values written to YAML validated, reviewed correctly, and had no runtime effect.

myopia_check.gap: Nothing owns concurrency admission at the target scale: well over a hundred agents at once, each with a declared maximum concurrency and each holding one isolation slot.
myopia_check.why_it_matters: Sandbox slots, gateway keys and lease stores are the shared choke points; without an admission queue as state, scale is discovered as a failure rather than declared as a bound.
myopia_check.proposed_owner: the agent composition for the declared bound, the isolation capability for the slot, and tenancy for whose quota the slot draws from
myopia_check.quote: The target scale is well over a hundred agents running at a time

myopia_check.gap: No state type covers the liveness of a grading instrument. The reference probes every instrument before the gate and refuses a plan when one is dead.
myopia_check.why_it_matters: A criterion that cannot answer within its service level turns a definition of done into an opinion at the worst possible moment - after spend.
myopia_check.proposed_owner: the judge, with the probe recorded on the plan card at gather time
myopia_check.quote: an instrument is dead, or a gate has no view

myopia_check.gap: Nothing owns the local GPU fleet's capacity as state, although a whole routing class is defined by it.
myopia_check.why_it_matters: A class that means free-and-local is a promise about capacity; when the cards are busy the class either queues, degrades or refuses, and none of those is currently a declared outcome.
myopia_check.proposed_owner: the model-access capability, as a routing input alongside budget remaining and the policy verdict (proposed)

myopia_check.gap: Proposed: nothing above holds the mapping between an interface version and the adapters that speak it, which is precisely what the impact map needs to be generated rather than written by hand.
myopia_check.why_it_matters: T7.4 asks the harness to show where the impacts are. A hand-written impact map is a document that goes stale; a generated one is a query over declared versions.
myopia_check.proposed_owner: the capability registry, holding the interface version each adapter record declares

open_questions.question: Is the run identifier minted once at intake and immutable for the life of the tree, or re-minted per unit with an explicit parent pointer?
open_questions.deciding_evidence: Run both shapes through a depth-3 tree that crosses the VM boundary and a simulated external-org hop; count the queries needed to reassemble the tree, and check whether any identifier reaches the external hop that should not.

open_questions.question: Does the durable-execution engine own the idempotency lease and the state journal, or does the state seam own both and the engine become a pure scheduler?
open_questions.deciding_evidence: Implement the state seam twice - once over a durable engine, once over a queue plus a state machine - and record which interface members only one of the two can satisfy.

open_questions.question: Can one in-process interception chain carry all seven cross-cutting concerns, or must budget and policy be enforced out of process because an in-process chain runs inside the code it governs?
open_questions.deciding_evidence: A red-team unit that deliberately attempts to bypass the chain - a direct provider call, an undeclared tool - and a count of how many bypasses each placement refuses.

open_questions.question: Is memory a third design-ourselves seam alongside dispatch and state, or a capability with an adoptable standard that this research simply did not find?
open_questions.deciding_evidence: A second search pass for a ratified memory-portability specification; absent one, the manifest records none found and the seam is designed here.

open_questions.question: Which enumeration of entries is normative - TARGET T1's three ways in, or T6.2's four entries - and where does the internal steering entry sit in the normative one?
open_questions.deciding_evidence: An owner decision; until then every entry-parity claim has to name which list it was checked against.

open_questions.question: Does the correlation record ride as an OTLP resource attribute, as baggage, as an event-body extension attribute, or as a dispatch request field - or as all four with a stated carrier per boundary?
open_questions.deciding_evidence: Emit one depth-3 run over all four carriers and measure which survives the agent boundary, the VM boundary and an event hop; the resource-attribute surface is the only one specified as unchangeable.

open_questions.question: What is the second adapter for human interaction? No swap candidate is recorded anywhere in the knowledge base for the approval surface.
open_questions.deciding_evidence: Name a second surface that breaks a different assumption than a phone on a private network - a queued decision with no live holder, for instance - and run the same ask through both.

open_questions.question: Is an agent profile a registry record or a document field? Both readings are consistent with what is recorded, and they differ on whether a profile can be rolled back independently of the plan that names it.
open_questions.deciding_evidence: Attempt a rollback of one agent version while a plan naming it is mid-run, under both readings, and see which one can express it.

open_questions.question: Should the effective-configuration attestation be a new capability row or a required behaviour of every existing adapter?
open_questions.deciding_evidence: Count how many of the nineteen components today can report their resolved configuration at all; if most cannot, it is a capability, and if most can, it is a conformance rule.
